title: Understanding One-hot Encoding
text: One-hot encoding is a way of representing categorical data as binary vectors. Each category is represented by a vector with a single high (1) bit and all other bits low (0).

title: One-hot Encoding of Whole DNA Strings
text: Consider the entire DNA string as a single category. How many unique DNA strings can be formed with $$3000$$ letters, each being one of T, G, C, A?

title: Calculate Dimensions for Whole DNA Strings
text: Calculate the number of possible DNA strings of length $$3000$$ using the formula for permutations with repetition.

title: One-hot Encoding of Codons
text: A codon is a sequence of $$3$$ DNA letters. How many unique codons can be formed?

title: Calculate Dimensions for Codons
text: Calculate the number of possible codons using the formula for permutations with repetition.

title: One-hot Encoding of 6-letter Combos
text: Consider sequences of $$6$$ DNA letters. How many unique sequences can be formed?

title: Calculate Dimensions for 6-letter Combos
text: Calculate the number of possible 6-letter sequences using the formula for permutations with repetition.

title: Understanding Bags-of-words
text: Bags-of-words is a model used to represent text data. It counts the occurrence of each word in a document, ignoring grammar and word order.

title: Calculate Dimensions for Bags-of-words
text: Consider how many unique words (or sequences) can be formed and counted in the DNA data.
